asks: how do I play Aurelion Sol
what's my job as asol
what does aurelion want from the game
asol game plan
say: You scale by stacking Stardust: farm and tag champions safely now to own late fights, or fly to a side fight when mid is quiet.
more: Cosmic Creator turns every damaging ability into Stardust, and Stardust permanently improves all your abilities. So a quiet lane where you keep landing spells is a lane you are winning.
Early you are slow and easy to jump on while channeling Breath of Light. Later the same channel melts a front line and Singularity controls a whole choke.
The trade-off is tempo: time spent stacking is time your side lanes play without you. Astral Flight lets you buy some of that back by crossing terrain to join a fight.
check: How many Stardust stacks you have, and whether the enemy mid can reach you while you stand still to channel.
breaks: If your team is losing every early fight without you, stop pure farming; push the wave and fly to the next fight, because a lost map leaves you nothing to scale into.

asks: when am I strong as asol
is six good on aurelion
what does my ult change
asol power spike
say: Level six gives you a real kill threat with Falling Star's stun, so look for one all-in, or hold it for their jungler's gank.
more: Falling Star stuns on impact, which finally lets you finish a full Breath of Light channel on someone who would otherwise walk away. It also grants Stardust for each champion it hits.
Used on a fight in river it stuns several people and stacks you faster. Held in lane it is your best answer to a dive.
Your bigger spike is not a level at all. It is Stardust building up through the mid game, so the ultimate is a tool for getting there, not the goal.
check: Their health and mana, whether they still have an escape, and where their jungler was last seen.
breaks: If their laner can dodge the star with a dash or blink, wait until that is used, or throw it on a grouped fight instead of a one on one.

asks: how do I trade as asol
how do I poke in lane aurelion
should I be using q on them
how do I win trades as aurelion sol
say: Breathe on them when no minion is in the way and they've used their spell, or just clear the wave with Singularity when they're threatening.
more: Breath of Light damages the first enemy it hits and only splashes reduced damage beyond it. Minions in the line take the main hit, so step to an angle where the champion is first.
You stand and channel, so you are the easy target during it. Trade right after they spend their main ability on the wave, when they cannot punish you for standing still.
Singularity damages and slowly pulls enemies toward its centre. Dropped on the wave it farms and stacks; dropped behind them it keeps them in your breath a little longer.
check: Whether minions block the line to them, and whether their main damage or crowd control ability was just used.
breaks: Against a champion who can jump on you at will, stop channeling in the open; farm with Singularity from range and take short breaths only near your tower.

when: your wave is cleared and a side lane fight or river objective is close
asks: should I roam as asol
when do I use astral flight to roam
can I fly bot
do I leave lane as aurelion
say: Shove the wave, then fly over the wall with Flight to the nearest fight, or stay and stack if your wave would crash under your tower.
more: Astral Flight crosses terrain, so you arrive from angles a walking mid laner cannot. While flying, Breath of Light has no cooldown or channel limit and deals more damage.
That makes you strongest arriving on a fight already started, breathing as you come in, not starting it yourself.
Every roam costs minions and Stardust from lane. Roam when the wave is pushed and something is actually happening; otherwise the lane stacks are worth more over ten minutes.
check: Where your wave is, whether the side lane enemies are pushed up, and where their mid laner went.
breaks: If their mid can shove and take tower plates while you are gone, or your side lane is already dead, stay and farm instead.

where do I stand in fights aurelion
who do I hit as asol
how do I teamfight aurelion sol
say: Stay behind your front line and breathe on whoever is closest, or open with Falling Star when they bunch up in a choke.
more: Late, your abilities are improved by all the Stardust you collected, so sustained damage on their front line is often enough. You do not need to reach the back line.
Singularity pulls enemies slowly toward its centre, which is strongest in a jungle corridor or a pit entrance where they cannot spread.
Keep Astral Flight for moving, not for arriving. Flying into them with no way out is how a late game carry gives away the game.
check: Where their divers and assassins are standing, and whether they have used the abilities that can reach you.
breaks: If they have several champions who jump the back line, stand further back and use Falling Star to stun the dive on you instead of starting the fight.

asks: how do I play Darius
what's darius supposed to do
darius game plan
what does darius want
say: You win long melee fights by stacking Hemorrhage to five, so force extended trades in lane, or freeze and deny them if they can kite you.
more: Every attack and damaging ability adds a bleed stack. At five stacks you gain massive attack damage, and Noxian Guillotine hits harder for each stack on the target.
So short trades favour them and long trades favour you. Your whole lane is about making a fight last a few seconds longer than they want.
Your weakness is reach. Apprehend is your only way to drag someone in, so in later fights you need speed, a flank or a target that comes to you.
check: How many bleed stacks they have, and whether Apprehend is available before you commit.
breaks: If they can step out before the stacks build, stop chasing; hold the wave near your tower so they have to walk up to you to farm.

asks: when is darius strong
is six my spike on darius
can I all in now darius
darius power spike
say: From level six a five-stack fight ends in Noxian Guillotine, so look for the all-in, or keep it ready to turn their jungler's gank around.
more: Noxian Guillotine is a leap that deals true damage, increased for each Hemorrhage stack. At full stacks it finishes targets that would otherwise walk away low.
You are already strong at the first few levels because the bleed and the Decimate heal win most early melee trades. Six just makes those wins lethal.
With their jungler nearby, a full-stack fight plus the enraged attack damage is one of the few ways a top laner wins a two on one.
check: Their health and bleed stacks, whether their escape is down, and whether their jungler could arrive mid-fight.
breaks: If they are healthy and can disengage before five stacks, do not open with the ultimate; trade until the stacks are there or wait for a gank.

how do I hit q on darius
when do I pull with e
darius trading pattern
say: Slow them with Crippling Strike and land the outer edge of Decimate for the heal, or pull with Apprehend first when they're standing far back.
more: Decimate's blade, the outer ring, deals more damage than the handle and heals you for each champion it hits. Standing on top of them wastes it, so take a half step back.
Crippling Strike slows, which makes the blade edge much easier to land. Apprehend also passively ignores part of their armour, so your attacks hurt from level one.
Using Apprehend to start means you have nothing to stop their retreat. Using it last means the trade may never start. Pick based on whether they come to you.
check: Whether Apprehend is up, how far the wave is from your tower, and whether they just used their escape.
breaks: If the wave is large and theirs, minion damage will lose you the long trade; hit the wave first and trade once it is even.

more: A ranged laner wins by hitting you for free while you walk at them. Near your own tower they must come closer to farm, and that is inside Apprehend's hook.
One pull is usually a full Hemorrhage fight, because a ranged champion who is slowed by Crippling Strike rarely gets back out.
You give up some minions early for this. The payoff is a lane where they can never fully relax, and a jungler visit that is nearly a guaranteed kill.
check: Where the wave is sitting, and whether they have a dash or blink available to escape the pull.
breaks: If they shove you under tower and still out-trade you, give up the idea of a solo kill; farm what you can with Decimate and wait for level six or your jungler.

darius teamfight

say: Stack the bleed on whoever is nearest and Guillotine the first low target, or stand by your carry and punish whoever dives them.
more: You cannot choose your target the way an assassin can. Hitting their front line still builds stacks and the enraged attack damage, which then carries onto the next target.
Apprehend pulls several enemies at once, so a pull through a choke as they walk in can start the fight on your terms.
Peeling is often the better half of the trade-off. Divers have to come into your range to reach your carry, which is exactly the fight you want.
check: Whether their carries have speed or dashes you cannot match, and where your own carry is standing.
breaks: If you are being kited with no way to close, stop walking forward; turn back and fight whoever is on your team's back line.

what's gnar's job
gnar game plan
what does gnar want to do
say: Small, you poke and kite from range; big, you engage and lock people on walls. Plan each fight around your Rage, or stall until it's full.
more: Rage builds while you are in combat. At maximum, your next ability turns you into Mega Gnar, with more survivability and a different set of spells.
Mini Gnar wins lane with boomerang slows and the bonus damage and speed from Hyper. Mega Gnar wins fights with GNAR! throwing people into terrain.
The skill is arriving at the right form. Too little Rage at an objective and you have no engage; full Rage wasted in lane and the fight starts without it.
check: Your Rage bar and how long until the next objective fight starts.
breaks: If a fight starts while you are small and far from full Rage, do not force an engage; kite, slow with the boomerang and peel until the bar fills.

what does gnar ult do for me at six
gnar power spike
can I kill them at six as gnar
say: At six a Mega transform near a wall is a kill with GNAR!, so fight near terrain at high Rage, or save it for a gank.
more: GNAR! throws everyone around you in a chosen direction. Anyone who hits a wall is stunned and takes bonus damage, so position decides whether it is a slow or a kill.
It only exists in Mega form. That means your level six threat comes and goes with the Rage bar, and a good opponent backs off while it is nearly full.
With your jungler arriving, a wall stun on the lane edge is long enough for both of you to finish, which makes you a strong lane to play around.
check: Your Rage, how close the enemy is to a wall, and where their jungler was last seen.
breaks: If they stay in the middle of the lane away from terrain, do not burn the form for a slow; poke as Mini and wait for the next full bar.

say: Poke with the boomerang and a few quick hits for the Hyper burst, then walk off, or keep Hop only for escaping when their jungler's unseen.
more: Boomerang Throw slows and returns to you; catching it cuts its cooldown, so step into its path on the way back.
Hyper adds bonus damage and gives you move speed, which is what lets you hit and leave before a melee laner answers.
Hop is both your gap closer and your only escape. Spending it to chase means a gank a few seconds later has a free kill, so decide which job it has.
check: Whether Hop is available, where the wave is, and how full your Rage is before you step forward.
breaks: If they have a dash that reaches you after you trade, shorten it to a boomerang only and farm from range until that dash is used.

more: Mini Gnar loses any trade a melee fighter gets to finish. Your win is many small hits they cannot return, with the boomerang slow keeping the gap.
Mega form flips it for a short window: you are tankier and have the hard crowd control. Fighters who dive a nearly full Rage bar often lose that trade.
Over several minutes the poke forces them to recall or farm from far back, which gives you plates and lets your jungler path away from top.
check: Whether their gap closer was just used, and how close your Rage is to full.

say: Build Rage on a wave before the fight, then Hop in big and throw them into a wall, or kite as Mini if the bar's low.
more: Mega Gnar's Crunch lands with an area hit and GNAR! throws everyone nearby in one direction. Into terrain that is a multi-person stun; in open ground it is only a slow.
So objective fights suit you, because pits and jungle corridors are full of walls. Mid lane in the open suits Mini Gnar's kiting more.
Transforming too early wastes the form before they group. Hitting minions or a camp just before the fight lets you arrive almost full and transform on the engage.
check: Your Rage bar, where the nearest wall is relative to their carries, and whether a flank is open.
breaks: If you arrive small with no Rage, your job changes: slow their front line with boomerangs and protect your carry until the form is ready.

what's jhin's job
jhin game plan

say: You're a long-range marksman with four heavy shots, so pick and follow up from distance, or play close behind your front line when fights get messy.
more: Whisper fires at a fixed rate and holds only four shots. You cannot out-attack other marksmen, so each shot and each ability has to be chosen.
In exchange you get reach: Deadly Flourish and Curtain Call hit from far outside normal fight range, and Captive Audience traps slow whoever walks over them.
That makes you better at starting and finishing fights than at standing still dealing damage through a long one. Play for picks and follow-up.
check: How many shots are left before your reload, and who on the enemy team can reach you.
breaks: If they have several divers, stop looking for long-range picks; stay beside your support and use traps at your own feet to slow whoever jumps in.

what does jhin ult do for me

say: Curtain Call lets you finish fleeing targets or help a fight from far away, so use it after trades, or hold it to cover mid.
more: Curtain Call fires four shots at extreme range that pass through minions and monsters but stop on the first champion. A low enemy walking away from a trade is no longer safe.
It also reaches river and sometimes mid from your lane. That means a skirmish at dragon can get your damage while you are still catching a wave.
You channel and cannot move while firing, so it is a tool for before or after the close fighting, not during it.
check: Whether an enemy can reach you while you channel, and whether a healthy champion is standing in front of your target.
breaks: If their front line can body-block the shots or someone can jump on you, use it only to finish, never to open.

more: Dancing Grenade can hit up to four targets and gains damage each time it kills. Thrown at a low minion beside the enemy, it arrives much stronger than cast directly.
With only four shots, their trade window is your reload. Step forward when your magazine is full and step back as it empties.
Deadly Flourish has huge range and passes through minions, so it follows up your support's engage from a safe distance.
check: Which minions are about to die near the enemy, and how many shots you have left.
breaks: If the enemy lane out-ranges you or has hard engage, stop walking up for auto trades; poke only with the grenade through the wave.

A slowed target in a corridor is the easiest Deadly Flourish and Curtain Call you will get, so the traps turn into picks before the fight starts.
Defensive traps are the other choice. Laid behind your team they cover a retreat if the objective goes badly.
check: Which entrances the enemy is likely to use, and whether they have vision that would reveal the traps.

jhin teamfight positioning

say: Hit whoever is safely in range and save Curtain Call to clean up the retreat, or open with it when they're stuck in a choke.
more: Your attack rate is fixed, so you cannot shred a tank quickly. Spread heavy single shots where they are safe and let abilities pick off the wounded.
Opening with Curtain Call softens a team that has to walk through a corridor toward you. Closing with it kills the ones who survive and run.
Reloading in the middle of a fight is your weakest moment. Know when the fourth shot is coming and be already stepping back.
check: Where their assassins and divers are, and whether you will be reloading when they engage.
breaks: If you are the only real damage and they are diving you, forget the long-range plan; stay near your support and shoot the nearest diver.

asks: how do I play Kled
what's kled's job
kled game plan
what does kled want to do
say: You're an early brawler whose charge starts fights across the map, so fight hard in lane, or look for the first skirmish to join.
more: Skaarl takes damage for you, so you effectively bring two health bars to a fight. When Skaarl's health runs out you dismount, your abilities change and you deal less damage to champions.
Mounted, you have a hook in Bear Trap on a Rope, a burst of attack speed in Violent Tendencies and a double dash in Jousting. That wins most early melee trades.
Chaaaaaaaarge!!! is why your lead travels. It carries you a long way and leaves a speed trail your team can follow.
check: Skaarl's health before every fight, and whether the enemy can simply walk away from you.
breaks: If you are dismounted, stop fighting; back off toward your tower or minions and only re-engage once you are mounted again.

more: Chaaaaaaaarge!!! sends you a long distance, gives a shield, and Skaarl rams the first enemy champion met. Allies who follow the trail gain speed.
Used on your laner it is a guaranteed start to an all-in. Used on the map it turns an even river fight into one where your team has an extra fighter.
Your early levels are already your strongest relative to most tops. Six is when that strength stops being stuck in one lane.
check: Where your wave is, where the fight would happen, and whether the enemy top laner can follow or punish your lane.
breaks: If leaving costs you a tower or a big wave and the fight is already lost, stay and use the charge on your laner instead.

more: Bear Trap on a Rope hooks a champion and, if they stay shackled briefly, yanks them toward you for extra damage. Jousting in keeps you close enough for the yank.
Violent Tendencies gives massive attack speed for four attacks, and the fourth hits harder. Trades that end before the fourth attack leave your best damage unused.
Jousting can be cast again to dash back through the target. That second dash is either more damage or your way out, not both.
check: Skaarl's health, whether Violent Tendencies is ready, and the size of the enemy wave.
breaks: If the trap misses, do not dash in after it; without the yank they can walk out of the four attacks and you lose the trade.

Coming from a side angle matters: Skaarl locks onto the first champion met, and from a flank that is more often a carry than a tank.
If their top laner left and you did not, a tower or plates is a fair trade for the objective. Deciding quickly is what makes either answer good.
check: Where your wave is, where the enemy top laner is, and whether your team is actually ready to fight.
breaks: If your team is not grouped or is already dead, do not charge into a lost fight; take the side lane gold instead.

say: You're the engage: charge onto a carry so your team rides the trail in behind you, or flank and wait if their front line blocks you.
more: The speed trail is as valuable as the ram. A whole team arriving at once on your target is what makes the engage work.
Because Skaarl hits the first champion in the way, a straight-line charge often lands on a tank. A side angle fixes that.
Late, you fall behind pure scaling champions in a long fight. Your value is the start: a fast pick on one target, then staying alive mounted.
check: Who is standing in the charge path, whether your team is close enough to follow, and Skaarl's health.
breaks: If your team has a better engage, hold the charge to follow it or to chase, and stay near your carry until then.

what's yi's job
master yi game plan

say: You're a farming carry with no crowd control: clear fast and take cleanup fights early, or gank only lanes that can lock the target for you.
more: Double Strike and the true damage from Wuju Style make your attacks scale with every item. Each camp you take moves you closer to the point where fights are yours.
Alpha Strike makes you untargetable and Highlander makes you immune to slows. Those let you finish fights; they do not let you start them.
The cost is the early map. While you farm, their jungler can gank freely, so tell your lanes to play safe and trade camps for it.
check: Which of your lanes have crowd control, and whether the enemy has saved a stun for you.
breaks: If their jungler is winning all three lanes while you farm, stop full clearing; countergank or take the objective on the opposite side.

more: Alpha Strike hits several units in a camp and Meditate restores health while reducing damage taken, so you can finish a full clear healthy without help.
You have no stun, slow or knock-up before level six. An early gank on a healthy laner mostly just shows where you are.
Six camps is about level four. Ending beside a river crab or a pushed-up lane gives you a choice between a safe objective and a cleanup.
check: Which side their jungler started, and whether a lane on your finishing side is pushed toward your tower.
breaks: If their jungler invades your second buff, do not fight him alone early; take the camps he left on his own side and keep farming.

more: You bring damage but nothing that holds a target. A laner's crowd control is what lets your attacks and Wuju Style's true damage actually land.
Alpha Strike gets you onto them, but if you open with it you have nothing left to follow a dash. Walking up first and saving it works better.
A failed gank costs you more than most junglers, because the camps you skipped were the whole plan. Pick ganks that are close to certain.
check: The enemy laner's health, whether their escape was used, and whether your laner still has their crowd control.
breaks: If the lane is pushed to the enemy tower, skip it; farm and come back when the wave has bounced toward your side.

more: Highlander gives move speed and attack speed and makes you immune to slows. Targets who used to walk away no longer can.
Because your damage comes through attacks, each finished attack item is a jump in strength, not a small step. Check your items against theirs before committing.
Farming to that item is safe but gives the map away. Fighting before it wins tempo only if someone else starts the fight for you.
check: Your items against their jungler's, and whether the enemy still holds a stun or root that Highlander does not stop.

Alpha Strike makes you untargetable for its duration. Saving it to dodge a key ability can be worth more than using it to arrive.
Meditate reduces damage taken, which can buy the moment your team needs. Peeling for your own carry is slower but far safer when they have many stuns.
check: Which enemy crowd control abilities have been used, and who is in range of your carry.

Consume damages a monster and heals you, which makes your clear healthy and gives you an edge when an objective is being finished.

You are one of the junglers who really can gank early, because the snowball's knock-up does not need levels or items.
The short clear puts you ahead of their jungler on the map but behind in camps. The full clear keeps you even and sets up the crabs at 2:55.

A lane pushed toward your tower gives you that distance behind them. A lane frozen at their tower gives you none.
Snowball Barrage roots champions hit once it finishes, so a walk-up gank still has crowd control. It is slower but hard to dodge at close range.
check: Where the wave is, whether the enemy has a dash to sidestep the snowball, and whether the river is warded.
